summary.text: The giant-impact hypothesis says the Moon formed after a Mars-sized protoplanet struck the young Earth about 4.5 billion years ago, and some of the ejected debris gathered into the Moon.
It accounts for several clues, such as lunar and Earth rocks having identical stable isotope ratios and the Earth–Moon system holding unusually high angular momentum.
Reginald Daly first proposed it in 1946, and at a 1984 conference on lunar origins in Kona, Hawaii, it emerged as the most favored hypothesis.

facts.label: Impactor's name
facts.value: Theia, mother of the Moon goddess Selene

items.prompt: Moon rocks brought back to Earth turn out to have stable isotope ratios identical to Earth's rocks. What does that most strongly suggest?

options.label: The Moon was captured from afar
Moon samples got contaminated here
The two share a common origin
All space rock has these ratios

items.explain: Identical stable isotope ratios in lunar and Earth rock imply that both came from the same source.

items.prompt: The Moon has a small iron core and is much less dense than Earth. How does a giant impact explain that?

options.label: The impactor's core merged with Earth's
The Sun boiled the Moon's iron away
The Moon grew from icy comet dust
Its iron leaked out through volcanoes

items.explain: Models show the impactor's core sinking into Earth and fusing with its core, so the Moon formed mostly from lighter crust and mantle fragments.

items.prompt: The Moon has fewer easily vaporized substances than Earth. How does the impact idea account for this?

options.label: Earth's oceans soaked them up
A magnetic field pushed them off
Lunar volcanoes buried them deep
They boiled off and weak gravity lost them

items.explain: These substances vaporize at lower temperatures, so a high-energy event could drive them off, and the Moon's smaller gravity could not recapture them while Earth's did.

items.prompt: Before the impact idea, what did George Darwin's 1898 explanation for the Moon say?

options.label: The Moon was captured passing by
A molten Moon was spun off Earth
The Moon broke off from Mars
The Moon grew from Earth's rings

items.explain: Darwin proposed that Earth and the Moon were once one body and that a molten Moon was spun from Earth by centrifugal forces.

items.prompt: Earth's spin, the Moon's spin and the Moon's orbit together hold far more momentum than other rocky planets have. What could have supplied the extra?

options.label: The pull of the Sun's gravity
Earth's magnetic field
A giant collision long ago
Slow cooling of Earth's core

items.explain: The Earth–Moon system's unusually high angular momentum is something a giant impact could provide.

items.prompt: Darwin calculated that the Moon once orbited much closer to Earth. What did lasers aimed at targets on the Moon later show?

options.label: It is drifting away from Earth
It is slowly falling toward Earth
Its distance never changes at all
It swings closer every century

items.explain: Laser ranging experiments confirmed Darwin's result that the Moon is drifting away from Earth.
